title: "It Is an Honour": York's Parvin Shortlisted for Best Curry House Award Again
excerpt: The Parvin in Haxby, winner of The Press Best Curry House in York award in 2017 and 2024, is shortlisted again — owner Safiqur Rahman calls the nomination itself an honour.
body:
• The Parvin Indian Restaurant, on York Road in Haxby, has been shortlisted for The Press Best Curry House in York award after hundreds of readers nominated their favourite spots.
  • Owner Safiqur Rahman, who has run The Parvin at its current site for more than 18 years, previously won the same award in 2017 and 2024.
  • The restaurant's Sunday buffet costs £15.90 per adult and runs from 3pm to 10pm; voting is by a slip included in each copy of The Press.
  • The Parvin also hosts charity quiz nights, now held twice a month, and will open on Christmas Day and over the New Year.

A York curry house that has already won its city's top reader award twice is in contention again. The Parvin Indian Restaurant, in York Road, Haxby, has been shortlisted for the Best Curry House in York award after hundreds of readers of The Press nominated their favourite spot in the city, according to The Press. Safiqur Rahman has run The Parvin at its current site for more than 18 years.

"To be nominated once again is an honour in itself."

— Safiqur Rahman, The Parvin

Speaking about the award, Rahman said the restaurant knows firsthand what the recognition can mean for a local business, having previously won The Press Best Curry House in York award in 2017 and 2024. "It introduces us to new customers, welcomes back familiar faces and reminds us why we love doing what we do," he said. "We would love nothing more than to bring the award home again, but whatever the outcome, our commitment remains the same: to serve excellent food, provide a warm welcome and continue giving our customers the very best experience possible."

What regulars come for

Among The Parvin's most popular offerings is the Sunday buffet, which costs £15.90 per adult and has attracted customers from across the area over the years, The Press reported. The restaurant opens for the buffet from 3pm till 10pm on Sundays, alongside its Monday to Saturday service. Dishes are served by eight full-time staff, along with part-time weekend staff. A separate Press review of the restaurant described generous portions and full-flavoured mains, and noted that The Parvin also won Best Takeaway in York in 2021 after securing the most votes from Press readers.

Rahman attributed the restaurant's record to ingredients and consistency. "We always pride ourselves on using the freshest & the highest quality ingredients combined with cooking skills & techniques which we have mastered over decades," he said. "Another main ingredient of our success has been our consistency, whether it's dining in with us, collecting a takeaway or having it delivered straight to your door we want every experience to be just as enjoyable as the last." The restaurant's own site is theparvin.co.uk.

Giving back, and how to vote

The Parvin also hosts a monthly charity quiz night, and its popularity has grown to the point that the restaurant now holds two per month for various causes, in partnership with local charities. "It's always a great night for curry and fun with friends or family for great causes," Rahman said. "It's our way of giving back to the local and surrounding areas that have helped build our success over many years." The restaurant will also open on Christmas Day and over the New Year.

Readers can vote for The Parvin by filling in a slip included in each copy of The Press. For a restaurant that has held the title in 2017 and 2024, a third win would confirm a long run rather than a breakthrough — and Rahman, by his own account, is content either way, as long as the food and the welcome stay the same.

nri_angle: A Bangladeshi-run York institution shortlisted for its city's best curry house title for a third time shows the depth of South Asian restaurants in Britain's local food culture.
